_comment: RFC-0001 slice B3a fixture: fetch-config + provenance stub for tests/corpus. Each entry under 'corpus' is {version, source, prepare?} -- the same shape RFC-0001 SS B.3's compat-manifest 'corpus' array records for provenance ({"version": ..., "source": "git:owner/repo@<sha>"}). 'source' is a well-formed but FAKE git:owner/repo@<40-hex-sha> placeholder -- this fixture corpus is hand-authored, never actually fetched. 'prepare' (present on exactly ONE entry here, 2.0.0) is an optional shell command the harvester runs BEFORE capturing that version's header snapshot, for libraries whose public headers are configure/generate outputs rather than checked-in files (mbedtls's config-dependent headers are RFC-0001 SS B.2's motivating case). Header-only, no-configure libraries -- like this fixture corpus itself -- need no 'prepare' at all; it's attached to one entry purely so slice B3's harvester (and any real fetch script modeled on this file) has a concrete example to target. See tests/corpus/README.md for the full classification narrative this corpus exists to exercise.
